doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Biagini, Duke and the Shaw band
title: Lead player or hot player
summary: Best says he could do a bit of each and discusses competition among trumpets.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Did you become known as a lead player or as a hot man, or somewhere in between?
Well I guess one of the compliments that I ever had, said during the war when they were drafting people, they said well I could, you know if you had to get down to one guy, I

would be the one, because I could do a little bit of each. I never had a real strong, you know, high notes, until after all the bands were through, and then I had my own group. Then I could play. But there was always somebody in that band that wanted to out-do you. Four trumpets wanted to blow you off the stand.
